settings.headline: Make your Senseless Selection
settings.subhead: Within the Senseless System, your selection has two parts — the format, and the strength. Here's how to make it.
settings.image_alt: An aesthetics practitioner and client choosing a Senseless strength — Clinical, Advanced, Professional

settings.headline: What the Senseless System is
settings.body: Most numbing is one product, sold one way. Senseless is built as a system — three formats and three strengths — so you can match what you use to what you're actually booking. Making your Senseless Selection means two choices, and neither is about buying the most expensive: the format (how it's applied and where) and the strength (how much the session asks for). The rest of this page walks you through both, then a by-procedure guide that puts them together.

settings.headline: Tell us about your appointment.
settings.intro: Three quick answers and we'll point you to the format and strength we'd reach for. A recommendation, not a rule — your practitioner has the final say.

settings.label: Cream
settings.note: Broad coverage, the default for most appointments and larger or simpler areas.

settings.label: Gel
settings.note: Holds exactly where you place it; for precise, facial work and longer sittings.

settings.label: Spray
settings.note: Fast, even, hands-off coverage for large or awkward-to-reach areas.

settings.headline: Selection one: the format
settings.intro: Format is about where the product goes and how it stays there. Three options:
settings.closer: If you're between cream and gel, the question is precision; between cream and spray, it's the size of the area.

settings.scale_clinical: The standard. Smaller areas, shorter or routine appointments, and anyone starting out. Fits the majority of sessions.
settings.scale_advanced: The considered upgrade. Larger areas, longer or more sensitive sessions. The deliberate step up when the session demands more.
settings.scale_professional: For the most demanding sessions. The longest, most sustained, most intensive work. More than most appointments need — and we'll tell you when.
settings.headline: Selection two: the strength
settings.body: Strength is separate from format — every format comes in all three. Which you choose depends on the session, not the procedure name: how large the area is, how long the appointment runs, how intense it is, and how sensitive your skin is. The three tiers are peers, not a ranking — each is matched to a different kind of session.
settings.note: Match the strength to the session you're actually having. If you're between two tiers, start with the one closer to your booking — you can choose differently next time.
settings.reassurance: Clinical isn't a lesser version of Professional, and Advanced isn't a half-measure. The three are matched to different sessions, not different levels of quality. Most people are on Clinical or Advanced because that's the right match for their booking.

settings.headline: Putting your selection together: what we recommend by procedure
settings.body: The honest version — the format and strength we'd point you to for each treatment, what's overkill, and what's rarely enough. This is a guide, so it covers injectables too; on the shop pages we keep those separate.
settings.closer: If you're unsure between two, go by the session — match the tier to how intensive the appointment is, and check with your practitioner.

settings.heading: Before you buy: a word most sellers skip
settings.body: For a lot of treatments the practitioner applies their own numbing as standard — microneedling especially. If yours does, you may not need to bring your own, and turning up already prepared without checking can get in the way. Self-applied numbing matters most where the practitioner doesn't provide it, or where you want extra preparation on top. A quick message before you book settles it.

settings.body:
• Senseless is a UK cosmetic numbing range by Matrix Health Group Ltd — not a medicine.

settings.question: What's the difference between Clinical, Advanced and Professional?
settings.answer: Different strengths of the same range — peers, not a ranking. Clinical is matched to shorter, routine sessions; Advanced to longer or more sensitive work; Professional to the longest, most demanding appointments. Each is built for a different kind of session.

settings.question: Is one tier better than the others?
settings.answer: No — the three tiers are peers, not a ranking. The right choice is the one matched to your appointment, not the most intensive; for many treatments, Clinical or Advanced is the match.

settings.question: How do I choose between cream, gel and spray?
settings.answer: Cream for broad coverage and most appointments, gel for precise facial work that needs to stay put, spray for large or awkward-to-reach areas.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product, not a medicine.

settings.headline: What the product is built to support.
settings.body:
Senseless is a topical preparation that supports comfort during your aesthetic appointment. Specific experience varies between clients — sensitivity, treatment area, procedure type, practitioner protocol. Many find prepared skin more comfortable than unprepared. The product isn't a substitute for a practitioner's care during your booking; it's the preparation step that sits before it.

You'll notice we don't lead with the active ingredient. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product, and the formulation details that matter are on the packaging and in the regulatory documentation that sits behind each SKU. What matters at the point of purchase is the system — strength matched to procedure, format matched to treatment area, brand built for aesthetics. The product specifics support that; they don't lead it.
